d: Watch this video as Firstpost explains how air quality across India has sharply deteriorated after Diwali celebrations, blanketing dozens of cities in a thick, hazardous haze. On November 13, Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) crossed the 400 mark and briefly entered the ‘severe’ category. According to Central Pollution Control Board data covering 286 cities, on November 12, Panchgaon in Haryana recorded the country's worst AQI at 388, while the national capital, Delhi, followed closely at 350. Haryana bears the heaviest burden, accounting for half of the 18 cities in the ‘Very Poor’…
